clue.text: Stand behind wife, one who can't be trusted

indicators.note: behind places the stand's letters after the wife's letter in the answer

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painting

explanation.surface: A husband standing loyally behind his wife turns out to be untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sly, shifty person, a figurative use from the animal's reputation for cunning.

clue.text: Sexy body with bust uncovered in book

indicators.note: uncovered strips the outer letters from each of the three words

explanation.surface: A racy description of an attractive body with exposed bust in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Exodus is the second book of the Old Testament, the Bible.

clue.text: Scarlatti's vacuous, say, and heated opera hero

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the composer's name keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by say
fried means heated in a pan

explanation.surface: A music critic finds a Scarlatti piece empty and overheated.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Scarlatti's is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried is the hero of Wagner's opera of that name in the Ring cycle.

clue.text: Failure back from staycation in plain Welsh town

indicators.note: in puts those letters inside the plain

parts.note: a llano is a grassy plain in South America
a dud is a failure

indicators.note: back from picks the last letter of staycation

explanation.surface: A disappointing staycation comes home to a dull Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: A staycation is a holiday at home rather than abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a seaside resort town in north Wales.

clue.text: Male dog in Manhattan?

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
to dog someone is to tail or follow them

explanation.surface: Asks whether a male dog is to be found in New York's Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like a noun but works as the verb to follow. Manhattan is a whisky-and-vermouth drink, hence the question mark for a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a mixed drink of whisky and vermouth, one example of this kind of drink.

clue.text: Blues singer's beginning to enter revolutionary field

parts.note: Che Guevara was a Marxist revolutionary

indicators.note: to enter puts that letter into the field

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a field

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of singer's

explanation.surface: A blues singer's career begins by entering a revolutionary field.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London football club nicknamed the Blues.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blues is the nickname of Chelsea Football Club, from its blue kit.

clue.text: My entertainment is endless in this island

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: is endless removes the final letter of the entertainment word

parts.note: fun is entertainment

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the entertainment on this island never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Worker this person rates

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
this person is the setter, I

explanation.surface: A worker sets out how this person rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rates' is a plural noun, speeds, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, the speed or pace of a piece of music.

clue.text: One shouldn't have entered run, tired when running

indicators.note: running means the letters are in motion, rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner who was tired should never have entered the race.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder is someone who goes in somewhere without permission.

clue.text: Chair, not a rocker, on which to find English judge

parts.note: Mods and Rockers were rival British youth tribes of the 1960s, so one who is not a rocker is a Mod
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: Seems to describe furniture: a chair that isn't a rocking chair, where an English judge sits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chair' looks like a noun but is the verb, to preside over a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To chair a debate is to moderate it, presiding and keeping order between speakers.

clue.text: Rather cold starter of relish with ham

indicators.note: starter of points to the opening letter of the word relish

parts.note: to ham is to overact, to emote

explanation.surface: A restaurant critic finds a starter of relish with ham a bit chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote manner is distant and aloof, a figurative coldness towards others.

clue.text: Beaten, as a criminal may be

definitions.meaning: a criminal may be ..., put in handcuffs on arrest

explanation.surface: A beating such as a criminal might receive.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuff is a slap, and to cuff is also slang for handcuffing a suspect.

clue.text: Counterfeit note passed by debtor in club

indicators.note: in puts the debtor's note inside the club's name

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club
an IOU is the note a debtor hands over acknowledging the debt

explanation.surface: A forged banknote is passed off by a man in debt at his club.
explanation.walkthrough: SPURS is Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club; the surface suggests a gentlemen's club.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurious means false or not genuine, as a counterfeit article is.

clue.text: Rising conflict for colonial government

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a jar is a clash or disagreement

explanation.surface: An uprising against colonial rule.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raj was British rule in India until 1947.

clue.text: State figure in empty Jaguars makes part of Ford

parts.note: Indiana is a US state

indicators.note: in puts the figure inside the emptied word
empty Jaguars leaves just the outside letters of that word

parts.note: one is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: Reads as car-industry talk: Jaguars and Ford, a carmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Ford is not the car company but the actor Harrison Ford.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana Jones is the archaeologist hero played by Harrison Ford, one of his film roles.

clue.text: After a drink, run the risk of fight with Henry?

parts.note: gin is a drink
to court danger is to run the risk of it

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drink and then risks a scrap with a man called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is Henry V, victor at Agincourt; 'After' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was the 1415 battle Henry V won against the French.

clue.text: Most unpleasant stink about commotion, by the way

indicators.note: about turns the stink letters round

parts.note: BO is body odour, a stink
a scene is a public commotion
St is street, a way

explanation.surface: A dreadful smell causes a commotion in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene can mean offensive or repugnant, so its superlative means most offensive.

clue.text: One who fixes taps in new cinema

indicators.note: in puts the taps inside the rearranged letters
new means the cinema letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taps are marked C and H, cold and hot

explanation.surface: A plumber fixes the taps in a newly built cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic repairs machinery and engines.

clue.text: Comment of tosser has aired, lost in translation

indicators.note: translation turns words into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something said on air has been lost in translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' is part of the fodder, not a deletion signal; the indicator is 'in translation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tossing a coin calls out the choice of outcomes for the person calling it.

clue.text: Runner bound to fail to 21

indicators.note: 21 down is the word for completing, so failing to complete it drops the last letter

parts.note: a skip is a bound, a leap

explanation.surface: An athlete is bound to fail to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is FINISH, so 'fail to 21' means lose the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a runner, as on a sledge or snowmobile.

clue.text: Couple dropping round confuse and talk rubbish

indicators.note: dropping means the round letter is removed

parts.note: a couple is two
O is round in shape
to addle is to confuse

explanation.surface: A couple go round confusing things and talking nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Twaddle as a verb means to speak silly, trivial nonsense.

clue.text: Possibly Polish language picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is spoken

parts.note: Finnish is the language of Finland

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a language overheard might be Polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is not the nationality but a coating, as a varnish.
explanation.definitionFit: A finish is a surface coating, and polish is one example.

clue.text: One's cracking allure and appeal, primarily?

definitions.text: One's cracking allure and appeal, primarily?

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the one's letters go inside the allure word

parts.note: charm is allure
One's is read as I'S, one being I plus is

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of appeal

explanation.surface: Wonders whether someone has great allure and appeal in the main.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is compelling personal attraction, the allure and appeal that draws others.

clue.text: University official losing the last page

indicators.note: losing the last drops the final letter

parts.note: a rector heads some universities

explanation.surface: A university official loses the last page.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book.

clue.text: Capital crossword setter involved in tête-à-tête?

indicators.note: involved in places the setter inside the sofa

parts.note: a tête-à-tête is an S-shaped sofa seating two facing each other
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A crossword setter in an intimate chat in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tête-à-tête' is the furniture, not a conversation, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Acclaim terrific red Italian has bottled

indicators.note: having something bottled means holding it inside, so the answer is contained in these words

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine Italian red wine that has been bottled.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit is praise or recognition given for an achievement.

clue.text: Bumf periodically about kindly charity

indicators.note: about means the alternate letters go around the kindly word
periodically takes every other letter of Bumf

parts.note: nice means kindly, pleasant

explanation.surface: Paperwork comes from a kindly charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Bumf is British slang for tedious paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: The United Nations Children's Fund is an international charitable relief organisation.

clue.text: This makes one go red, one twice cut off

indicators.note: off signals the letters going wrong, so they are shuffled

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
twice asks for the Roman one a second time, another I

explanation.surface: Something that makes a person blush, cut off twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' means urinate; 'off' shuffles RED, II and CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A diuretic is a drug or drink that increases urine output, so it sends someone to the toilet.

clue.text: A rebel welcoming officer's commendation

indicators.note: welcoming means taking the officer's letters inside

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion against Henry VI in 1450
COL abbreviates colonel, an officer; the 's links to what follows

explanation.surface: A rebel embraces an officer's praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the 1450 Kentish rebellion in England.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or expression of praise, a commendation.

clue.text: Make an impression in Tiffany's jacket that's short

indicators.note: in puts the impression word inside those outer letters
a jacket is the outer covering, so only the outside letters of Tiffany's

parts.note: to etch is to cut an impression into a surface

explanation.surface: Someone makes an impression in a short Tiffany jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-tempered and tetchy both describe irritability and quick annoyance.
